summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted to the medicine service after transfer from a psychiatric facility due to altered mental status and lethargy. She had been heavily medicated with multiple psychiatric drugs, leading to toxic encephalopathy. Workup revealed no acute intracranial or pulmonary pathology. Her mental status improved significantly after discontinuation of polypharmacy, retaining only lamotrigine and clonazepam. She experienced migraine-like headaches treated with Fiorinal, transient diarrhea that resolved spontaneously, and intermittent facial pain without organic cause. Psychiatry confirmed the need for continued inpatient care, and she was medically cleared after nine days. She was discharged to an extended psychiatric care facility with a simplified medication regimen and plans for ongoing mental health treatment.
